arugula.name: Arugula
arugula.description: Grows fast, takes up little space. When the first field is established, it provides the quickest contribution to colony nutrition. Low nutritional value but maintains morale.

cress.name: Cress
cress.description: The fastest-growing plant in the colony. Regular ventilation is essential against mold risk. The first food source to mature in emergency hunger situations.

lettuce.name: Lettuce
lettuce.description: High water consumption but a noticeable morale boost. Balances the mood of colonists who eat the same food for long periods. Growing it without a water filter is risky.

spinach.name: Spinach
spinach.description: Has the highest energy contribution among leafy greens. Rich in iron; carries critical nutritional value for colonists living in enclosed environments for long periods.

green_onion.name: Green Onion
green_onion.description: Can grow even in deep modules with its low light requirement. The safest option for farming in the early period when access to solar panels is unavailable.

tomato.name: Tomato
tomato.description: The colonists' favorite. Has the highest morale contribution among vegetables; preserves psychological balance during long enclosed living periods. Requires high light, a light panel is mandatory.

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.description: High satiety value but spoils quickly after harvest. If storage conditions are poor, waste is inevitable. Large-scale cultivation is not recommended without a cold storage system.

pepper.name: Pepper
pepper.description: Carries the highest morale value among all foods. One of the rare flavor sources that keeps colonist morale up during long and monotonous survival periods.

potato.name: Potato
potato.description: The colony's primary calorie source. Grows in every module with its low light requirement and does not spoil for a long time. Indispensable in large colonies; the only plant that prevents hunger crises.

onion.name: Onion
onion.description: Low water and light requirements, long-lasting. A reliable reserve food during scarce resource periods. Increases energy efficiency when consumed together with other foods.

corn.name: Corn
corn.description: The most versatile grain with its high morale and satiety balance. Despite its long growth period, it can be stored for a long time without spoiling after harvest.

wheat.name: Wheat
wheat.description: The plant with the highest satiety value. Requires little water but the pest risk is real; an insect outbreak in enclosed modules can destroy the entire stock. Regular inspection is mandatory.

rice.name: Rice
rice.description: The most nutritious plant but one of the highest water consumers. Growing it without a water recycling unit creates serious resource pressure. Ideal for a mature colony, risky for the early period.

lentil.name: Lentil
lentil.description: Stands out among legumes for its energy value. Low morale contribution; colonists may complain about eating lentils for long periods. Balance with other plants for a varied diet.

chickpea.name: Chickpea
chickpea.description: The most efficient legume with the highest energy value and lowest water requirement. The long harvest period requires patience, but once stocked it provides long-term security for the colony.

bean.name: Bean
bean.description: Despite its high nutritional value, one of the plants with the lowest morale contribution. Meets the basic need but must be supported with other plants for colonist satisfaction.

pea.name: Pea
pea.description: The fastest-growing among legumes. A reliable food of the transition period with its balanced satiety-energy-morale values. Fills the gap during periods when long-lasting products are not yet ready.

sunflower.name: Sunflower
sunflower.description: Requires very high light but almost no water. Does not spoil for an extremely long time after harvest; an ideal stock food for long journeys or quarantine periods. Its oil can also be used as fuel and grease.
